title: A continuous profinite map has a finite-field coset rectangle
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] with the extended norm topology, and a finite intermediate field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $G$ be a profinite group, meaning a compact Hausdorff topological group whose open subgroups form a neighbourhood basis of the identity. Let $m\geq1$ and $d\geq0$ be integers, and give $G^m$ and $\Omega^d$ their product topologies. For every continuous function $f:G^m\to\Omega^d$ there exist a finite intermediate extension $E\subseteq F\subseteq\Omega$, an open subgroup $H\subseteq G$, and elements $a_0,\ldots,a_{m-1}\in G$ such that
$$f(h_0a_0,\ldots,h_{m-1}a_{m-1})\in F^d\subseteq\Omega^d\qquad(h_0,\ldots,h_{m-1}\in H).$$
The subgroup need not be normal. No equivariance or cocycle condition on $f$, no completeness of $\Omega$, and no finite generation of $G$ is assumed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent arithmetic expansion; returned local-cocycle proof steps 2–3: closed finite-field exhaustion, Baire on G^m, and one common left-coset rectangle. Baire source: Stacks Tag 0CQN, topology.tex, lemma-baire-category-locally-compact; countability source: literature/stanford-weil2-seminar/L19.pdf, Proposition 1.1.9, p. 3. Neither source states this precise rectangle assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-algcl-countable-closed-finite-cover] to the given $\ell,\Omega,E$, obtaining increasing closed finite intermediate fields $F_j\supseteq E$ covering $\Omega$. Put $X=G^m$ and $A_j=\{x\in X:\forall r<d,\ f(x)_r\in F_j\}$. Each coordinate of $f$ is continuous, so $A_j$ is the finite intersection of inverse images of the closed set $F_j$, hence closed. For each $x$, choose an index for each of the finitely many coordinates of $f(x)$ and take their maximum; increasingness gives $x\in A_j$. If $d=0$, use $j=0$ and the empty intersection $A_0=X$. Thus $X=\bigcup_{j\geq0} A_j$.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, first bullet, p. 3; agent adaptation from matrix coefficients to an arbitrary finite coordinate family, using the existing closed-cover node.

proof.text: The product $X$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-tychonoff-product-quasi-compact]. It is Hausdorff: distinct tuples differ in a coordinate, and disjoint coordinate neighbourhoods pull back to disjoint neighbourhoods. It is nonempty, containing $(1,\ldots,1)$, and locally compact, since the whole quasi-compact space is a neighbourhood of every point. Apply [lem-sfb-baire-closed-cover-interior] to the nonempty full subspace $Y=X$ and the closed cover $(A_j)_{j\in\mathbf N}$. It gives $j$ and $a=(a_0,\ldots,a_{m-1})\in\operatorname{Int}_X(A_j)$.

source.place: Tag 0CQN, lemma-baire-category-locally-compact, closed-cover consequence; product compactness via the cited Tychonoff node.

proof.text: By the finite product topology choose open neighbourhoods $U_r$ of $a_r$ with $\prod_{r<m}U_r\subseteq\operatorname{Int}_X(A_j)$. Right translation by $a_r^{-1}$ is a homeomorphism: the map and its inverse are continuous by continuity of group multiplication. Thus $U_ra_r^{-1}$ is an identity neighbourhood. By the assumed open-subgroup basis choose an open subgroup $H_r\subseteq U_ra_r^{-1}$. The finite intersection $H=\bigcap_{r<m}H_r$ is an open subgroup. For every $h_r\in H$, one has $h_ra_r\in U_r$, so $(h_0a_0,\ldots,h_{m-1}a_{m-1})\in A_j$ and its image lies in $F_j^d$. Take $F=F_j$.

Small cases checked: trivial G, d=0, constant f, m=1 with G=Z_ℓ and f(g)=gα. The only citer, local-norm-algcl-cocycle-descent step 2 (m=n+1), needs exactly this.
